description: This Python script analyzes a Git repository to identify downstream commits that are not upstream and are visible in the diff, focusing on non-merged, non-reverted changes. It provides functions to find commits exclusive to downstream branches relative to upstream branches, including specifics per file.

classes.name: CommitFinder
classes.description: A class used to find commit hashes that introduced changes for a specific file between upstream and downstream branches.

methods.name: git(args)
methods.description: Runs a git command with provided arguments and returns its output.

methods.name: __init__(self, working_dir, upstream, downstream)
methods.description: Initializes a CommitFinder instance with working directory and branch info.

methods.name: __call__(self, filename)
methods.description: Returns a set of commit hashes that have modified a specific file between upstream and downstream branches.

methods.name: find_insertion_commits(upstream, downstream, working_dir)
methods.description: Finds commits that insert lines in the diff between upstream and downstream branches for all files.

methods.name: find(upstream, downstream, working_dir)
methods.description: Identifies all downstream commits that are not present upstream and are visible in the diff.

methods.name: main()
methods.description: Entry point for command-line execution, parses arguments and outputs the list of downstream-only commits.
